steps: Given: Isotopic abundances of krypton: Kr-80 = 2.0%, Kr-82 = 12.0%, Kr-83 = 12.0%, Kr-84 = 57.0%, Kr-85 = 17.0%.
Required: Relative atomic mass of krypton.
Formula: Relative atomic mass = (sum of [isotopic mass number × relative isotopic abundance]) / 100.
Substitution: Relative atomic mass of Kr = (80 × 2.0 + 82 × 12.0 + 83 × 12.0 + 84 × 57.0 + 85 × 17.0) / 100.
Working: Relative atomic mass of Kr = 8370 / 100 = 83.7.
Result: Relative atomic mass of krypton = 83.7.
Given: Relative atomic mass of chlorine = 35.45; relative isotopic abundance of Cl-37 = 24.23%.
Relative isotopic abundance of the light isotope of chlorine = 100% − 24.23% = 75.77%.
Required: Relative atomic mass of the light isotope of chlorine.
Formula: Relative atomic mass of chlorine = (mass of light isotope × its abundance + mass of Cl-37 × its abundance) / 100.
Result: Relative atomic mass of the light isotope of chlorine = 34.95.
The nucleus contains protons and neutrons, each having a mass of approximately 1 atomic mass unit.
The mass of an electron is very small compared with the mass of a proton or a neutron.
Therefore, the mass of the electrons is negligible compared with the mass of the nucleus.
Hence, almost all the mass of an atom is concentrated in its nucleus.
items.finalAnswer: Almost all the mass of an atom is concentrated in its nucleus because electrons have negligible mass compared with protons and neutrons.

steps: The number of protons in the nucleus of an atom is called its atomic number.
Each element has a different atomic number, that is, a different number of protons in its nucleus.
Therefore, elements are different from one another because they have different numbers of protons.
items.finalAnswer: Elements differ from one another because their atoms have different numbers of protons in the nucleus.

steps: Given: Mass number, A = 210; atomic number, Z = 83.
Required: Number of neutrons, N.
Formula: N = A − Z.
Substitution: N = 210 − 83.
Working: N = 127.
Result: The number of neutrons in ²¹⁰₈₃Bi is 127.
Tritium has one proton and two neutrons in its nucleus.
Its nucleus is unstable.
An unstable nucleus emits radiations to become more stable.
Therefore, tritium is radioactive.
items.finalAnswer: Tritium is radioactive because its nucleus is unstable and emits radiation.

steps: An atom absorbs energy when an electron jumps from a lower energy level to a higher energy level.
An atom evolves (emits) energy when an electron jumps from a higher energy level to a lower energy level.
The energy absorbed or emitted is equal to the difference between the two energy levels.
items.finalAnswer: An atom absorbs energy when an electron moves to a higher energy level and emits energy when it returns to a lower energy level.

steps: The second shell is farther from the nucleus than the first shell.
The attraction of the nucleus for an electron becomes weaker as its distance from the nucleus increases.
An electron in the second shell therefore has greater energy than an electron in the first shell.
items.finalAnswer: The energy of an electron increases from the first shell to the second shell because the second shell is farther from the nucleus.
